text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 3

You and the appointed candidate are both men, so an all-male panel can't plausibly explain why you lost to him. Raising it would weaken your credibility on the points that actually matter.

Those points are strong. On formal criteria you appear better qualified: a master's in educational leadership versus "courses," plus five years of actual leadership experience. If the post required or weighted leadership education and experience, the panel needs to justify ranking him above you — teaching years alone usually won't do it.

Press the unanswered request instead. Silence after two weeks is likely a breach of the duty to give reasons. Send a written follow-up with a deadline, ask for the panel's assessment and scoring, and note that any appeal deadline runs from when you receive them.
